also: pardon me for what I said

terms.gloss: given for “pardon me for what I said”
terms.comment: The future perfect dīxerō looks forward, but what is pardoned is already said. Ignōscere takes quod with the indicative of what was done (velim mihi ignōscās, quod ad tē scrībō tam multa totiēs, Cic. Att. 7.12.3, Lewis & Short), so Ignōsce mihi, quod ita dīxī.

sources: Lewis & Short: ignosco
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, supplied PDF (printed page numbers): pp. 97, 27; p. 311.

phrases.english: please forgive me for writing to you so much and so often
